layer-boundary.title: SMT101: A layer imports a layer outside its `may_depend_on` allowlist.
layer-boundary.description: A layer imports a layer outside its `may_depend_on` allowlist. Layers only stay replaceable and testable when dependencies point in one direction. An application service that imports infrastructure cannot be used without the database, HTTP client or framework behind it. With architecture.imports.transitive, the allowlist also applies to every reachable layer, including paths through allowed layers and helpers. Indirect findings include a shortest import chain. Repair: Depend on an abstraction (a port) owned by the importing layer or an allowed layer, and wire the concrete implementation in the composition root.
layer-boundary.markdownDescription:
**SMT101 — layer-boundary**

A layer imports a layer outside its `may_depend_on` allowlist.

Layers only stay replaceable and testable when dependencies point in one direction. An application service that imports infrastructure cannot be used without the database, HTTP client or framework behind it. With architecture.imports.transitive, the allowlist also applies to every reachable layer, including paths through allowed layers and helpers. Indirect findings include a shortest import chain.

**Problem**
```python
# voice/application/session.py
from gateway.features.voice.infra.sql import SqlVoiceSessionRepository
```

**Preferred**
```python
# voice/application/session.py
from gateway.features.voice.application.ports import VoiceSessionRepository

# gateway/bootstrap.py wires SqlVoiceSessionRepository to the port
```

Depend on an abstraction (a port) owned by the importing layer or an allowed layer, and wire the concrete implementation in the composition root.

Run `smelt explain layer-boundary` for details.

cross-feature-import.title: SMT102: A feature imports another feature outside the allowed layer pairs.
cross-feature-import.description: A feature imports another feature outside the allowed layer pairs. Features are independent slices. Direct imports between them couple release cycles and make it impossible to reason about one feature in isolation. With architecture.imports.transitive, allowed pairs also apply to all reachable feature modules, with a shortest import chain as evidence. Repair: Go through an allowed relationship, declare an intended one explicitly (`allow: [{from: orders.application, to: billing.application}]`), move the shared concept into a `shared` package, or merge the features.
cross-feature-import.markdownDescription:
**SMT102 — cross-feature-import**

A feature imports another feature outside the allowed layer pairs.

Features are independent slices. Direct imports between them couple release cycles and make it impossible to reason about one feature in isolation. With architecture.imports.transitive, allowed pairs also apply to all reachable feature modules, with a shortest import chain as evidence.

**Problem**
```python
# billing/infra/charges.py
from gateway.features.voice.infra.sql import CallLog
```

**Preferred**
```python
# billing/application/charges.py
from gateway.features.voice.application.api import CallSummaryQuery
```

Go through an allowed relationship, declare an intended one explicitly (`allow: [{from: orders.application, to: billing.application}]`), move the shared concept into a `shared` package, or merge the features.

Run `smelt explain cross-feature-import` for details.

third-party-denied.title: SMT103: A layer imports a third-party package its `third_party` policy does not allow.
third-party-denied.description: A layer imports a third-party package its `third_party` policy does not allow. Inner layers should not know about frameworks, drivers or SDKs. Keeping them out makes the core portable and cheap to test. With architecture.imports.transitive, the importing layer's policy also applies to packages reached through project modules, such as domain -> shared.utils -> sqlalchemy. A shortest chain includes each import's source line. External packages are leaves: their own source is not scanned. Standard-library imports remain allowed. Repair: Move the code that needs the package into a layer that allows it and expose it through a port, or extend the layer's `third_party` policy.
third-party-denied.markdownDescription:
**SMT103 — third-party-denied**

A layer imports a third-party package its `third_party` policy does not allow.

Inner layers should not know about frameworks, drivers or SDKs. Keeping them out makes the core portable and cheap to test. With architecture.imports.transitive, the importing layer's policy also applies to packages reached through project modules, such as domain -> shared.utils -> sqlalchemy. A shortest chain includes each import's source line. External packages are leaves: their own source is not scanned. Standard-library imports remain allowed.

**Problem**
```python
# voice/domain/session.py
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped
```

**Preferred**
```python
# voice/domain/session.py
from dataclasses import dataclass
```

Move the code that needs the package into a layer that allows it and expose it through a port, or extend the layer's `third_party` policy.

Run `smelt explain third-party-denied` for details.

import-cycle.title: SMT104: Import cycles between features, between layers, or between sibling modules.
import-cycle.description: Import cycles between features, between layers, or between sibling modules. Cycles mean two parts can only be understood, tested and changed together. They also cause import-order bugs at runtime, unless one edge is imported only under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`; such cycles are marked `(type checking only)`. Imports that other rules already forbid (SMT101, SMT102, SMT106) and outbound imports from declared wiring are left out, so a cycle report means the cycle is built entirely from ordinary allowed dependencies. Repair: Break one edge of the cycle: extract the shared piece into a module both can import, invert one dependency behind an abstraction, or merge the parts.
import-cycle.markdownDescription:
**SMT104 — import-cycle**

Import cycles between features, between layers, or between sibling modules.

Cycles mean two parts can only be understood, tested and changed together. They also cause import-order bugs at runtime, unless one edge is imported only under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`; such cycles are marked `(type checking only)`. Imports that other rules already forbid (SMT101, SMT102, SMT106) and outbound imports from declared wiring are left out, so a cycle report means the cycle is built entirely from ordinary allowed dependencies.

**Problem**
```python
# billing/application/invoices.py
from gateway.features.voice.application import calls
# voice/application/calls.py
from gateway.features.billing.application import invoices
```

**Preferred**
```python
# voice/application/calls.py publishes an event;
# billing/application/invoices.py subscribes to it.
```

Break one edge of the cycle: extract the shared piece into a module both can import, invert one dependency behind an abstraction, or merge the parts.

Run `smelt explain import-cycle` for details.

shared-imports-feature.title: SMT105: A `shared` module or a central module (`architecture.modules`) imports a feature module.
shared-imports-feature.description: A `shared` module or a central module (`architecture.modules`) imports a feature module. Shared code and central layers such as a platform package are importable by every feature. If they depend on a feature, every feature transitively depends on that feature and the slices collapse. With architecture.imports.transitive, paths through arbitrary project helpers and facades are checked and reported with a shortest import chain. Repair: Move the needed concept into shared, or move the shared code into the feature.
shared-imports-feature.markdownDescription:
**SMT105 — shared-imports-feature**

A `shared` module or a central module (`architecture.modules`) imports a feature module.

Shared code and central layers such as a platform package are importable by every feature. If they depend on a feature, every feature transitively depends on that feature and the slices collapse. With architecture.imports.transitive, paths through arbitrary project helpers and facades are checked and reported with a shortest import chain.

**Problem**
```python
# gateway/shared/money.py
from gateway.features.billing.domain import Currency
```

**Preferred**
```python
# gateway/shared/money.py
class Currency: ...
```

Move the needed concept into shared, or move the shared code into the feature.

Run `smelt explain shared-imports-feature` for details.

composition-root-leak.title: SMT106: A module imports the composition root or a declared wiring module.
composition-root-leak.description: A module imports the composition root or a declared wiring module. Wiring belongs in one place. When features reach for the container or the bootstrap module, construction logic spreads and dependencies become hidden. With architecture.imports.transitive, paths through arbitrary project modules are checked and reported with a shortest import chain. Repair: Receive dependencies through constructor parameters and register them in the composition root.
composition-root-leak.markdownDescription:
**SMT106 — composition-root-leak**

A module imports the composition root or a declared wiring module.

Wiring belongs in one place. When features reach for the container or the bootstrap module, construction logic spreads and dependencies become hidden. With architecture.imports.transitive, paths through arbitrary project modules are checked and reported with a shortest import chain.

**Problem**
```python
# voice/application/session.py
from gateway.main import container
```

**Preferred**
```python
# voice/application/session.py
class StartSession:
    def __init__(self, sessions: VoiceSessionRepository) -> None: ...
```

Receive dependencies through constructor parameters and register them in the composition root.

Run `smelt explain composition-root-leak` for details.

private-module-import.title: SMT107: Code outside a contracted package imports a private implementation module.
private-module-import.description: Code outside a contracted package imports a private implementation module. Explicit entry points keep callers coupled to a package's supported interface. Internal imports and intentional symbol re-exports through public facades remain valid. Wiring and composition roots still obey these contracts. Layer and feature policies apply independently. Repair: Import through one of the contract's public entry points. Expose a deliberate API there if needed, or explicitly revise the contract. Public entries are exact module patterns; add .** only when the whole subtree is intentionally public.
private-module-import.markdownDescription:
**SMT107 — private-module-import**

Code outside a contracted package imports a private implementation module.

Explicit entry points keep callers coupled to a package's supported interface. Internal imports and intentional symbol re-exports through public facades remain valid. Wiring and composition roots still obey these contracts. Layer and feature policies apply independently.

**Problem**
```python
# app/client.py
from app.orders.storage import OrderStore
```

**Preferred**
```python
# app/client.py
from app.orders.api import place_order
```

Import through one of the contract's public entry points. Expose a deliberate API there if needed, or explicitly revise the contract. Public entries are exact module patterns; add .** only when the whole subtree is intentionally public.

Run `smelt explain private-module-import` for details.

package-import-fanout.title: SMT108: One caller imports many implementation modules of the same package.
package-import-fanout.description: One caller imports many implementation modules of the same package. Repeated imports of neighboring implementation modules can indicate a missing package API. This is an opt-in design hint, not proof of poor architecture. Count distinct target modules per source file and contracted package, not statements, symbols, or imports across the whole repository. Repair: Consider exporting the caller's supported API from the package facade. Check dependency direction and cycles before changing exports. If these independent dependencies are intentional, retain them or adjust the advisory threshold. Declare public: ['.'] to enforce facade-only imports.
package-import-fanout.markdownDescription:
**SMT108 — package-import-fanout**

One caller imports many implementation modules of the same package.

Repeated imports of neighboring implementation modules can indicate a missing package API. This is an opt-in design hint, not proof of poor architecture. Count distinct target modules per source file and contracted package, not statements, symbols, or imports across the whole repository.

**Problem**
```python
# caller.py
from app.users.application.get_user import GetUser
from app.users.application.update_user import UpdateUser
from app.users.application.delete_user import DeleteUser
```

**Preferred**
```python
# caller.py, after deliberate facade exports are defined
from app.users.application import DeleteUser, GetUser, UpdateUser
```

Consider exporting the caller's supported API from the package facade. Check dependency direction and cycles before changing exports. If these independent dependencies are intentional, retain them or adjust the advisory threshold. Declare public: ['.'] to enforce facade-only imports.

Run `smelt explain package-import-fanout` for details.

unknown-layer.title: SMT301: A feature contains a package or module outside the declared layers.
unknown-layer.description: A feature contains a package or module outside the declared layers. Code outside the layer grid is invisible to every layer rule: voice/models/ or voice/helpers.py can import anything and be imported by anything. A feature's __init__.py is fine, and not every feature needs every layer. Repair: Move the code into a declared layer, or declare its package as a layer if the architecture has a distinct responsibility for it.
unknown-layer.markdownDescription:
**SMT301 — unknown-layer**

A feature contains a package or module outside the declared layers.

Code outside the layer grid is invisible to every layer rule: voice/models/ or voice/helpers.py can import anything and be imported by anything. A feature's __init__.py is fine, and not every feature needs every layer.

**Problem**
```python
voice/
  domain/
  application/
  models/      # not a layer
  helpers.py   # in no layer
```

**Preferred**
```python
voice/
  domain/
    models.py
  application/
```

Move the code into a declared layer, or declare its package as a layer if the architecture has a distinct responsibility for it.

Run `smelt explain unknown-layer` for details.

forbidden-package-name.title: SMT302: A package or module name is listed in structure.forbidden_names.
forbidden-package-name.description: A package or module name is listed in structure.forbidden_names. Names like utils or helpers describe nothing, so everything fits in them. They grow into grab bags that every layer imports. Repair: Name the module after what it does, or move each function next to its callers.
forbidden-package-name.markdownDescription:
**SMT302 — forbidden-package-name**

A package or module name is listed in structure.forbidden_names.

Names like utils or helpers describe nothing, so everything fits in them. They grow into grab bags that every layer imports.

**Problem**
```python
voice/application/utils.py
```

**Preferred**
```python

```

Name the module after what it does, or move each function next to its callers.

unclassified-module.title: SMT305: A module maps to no feature, layer, shared set or composition root.
unclassified-module.description: A module maps to no feature, layer, shared set or composition root. Unclassified modules are exempt from layer and feature boundary checks: a domain module may import them. Composition-root/wiring restrictions and configured cycle checks still apply. Central code such as a database or storage package belongs to a layer via architecture.modules. Root packages with no classified module at all (libraries) are skipped. Repair: Give the package a layer under architecture.modules, list it in architecture.shared or composition_root, or move it into a feature.
unclassified-module.markdownDescription:
**SMT305 — unclassified-module**

A module maps to no feature, layer, shared set or composition root.

Unclassified modules are exempt from layer and feature boundary checks: a domain module may import them. Composition-root/wiring restrictions and configured cycle checks still apply. Central code such as a database or storage package belongs to a layer via architecture.modules. Root packages with no classified module at all (libraries) are skipped.

**Problem**
```python
gateway/
  platform/db.py    # neither shared, a layer nor a feature
```

**Preferred**
```python
# smelt.yaml
architecture:
  modules:
    gateway.platform: infrastructure
```

Give the package a layer under architecture.modules, list it in architecture.shared or composition_root, or move it into a feature.

Run `smelt explain unclassified-module` for details.

incomplete-coverage.title: SMT306: Strict coverage found source outside the architecture policy or an exclusion without a reason.
incomplete-coverage.description: Strict coverage found source outside the architecture policy or an exclusion without a reason. A passing architecture check is only useful when production code cannot silently escape its package selection or classification. Strict coverage inventories source roots and Python workspace members independently of project.root_packages. Pure package facades do not need their own layer. Repair: Select missing production packages and assign their architecture role. Move unclassified implementation into an existing layer. Deliberately excluded code needs project.exclude entries with path and reason. Coverage gaps cannot be hidden by debt, inline ignores or a narrowed check.
incomplete-coverage.markdownDescription:
**SMT306 — incomplete-coverage**

Strict coverage found source outside the architecture policy or an exclusion without a reason.

A passing architecture check is only useful when production code cannot silently escape its package selection or classification. Strict coverage inventories source roots and Python workspace members independently of project.root_packages. Pure package facades do not need their own layer.

**Problem**
```yaml
# smelt.yaml
project:
  root_packages: [backend]
  coverage: strict
# A new workspace library exists but is not selected or classified.
```

**Preferred**
```yaml
# smelt.yaml
project:
  root_packages: [backend, client]
  source_roots: [backend/src, libs/client/src]
  coverage: strict
architecture:
  modules: {client: infrastructure}
```

Select missing production packages and assign their architecture role. Move unclassified implementation into an existing layer. Deliberately excluded code needs project.exclude entries with path and reason. Coverage gaps cannot be hidden by debt, inline ignores or a narrowed check.

Run `smelt explain incomplete-coverage` for details.

missing-required-module.title: SMT307: A package contract is missing a required module or public entry point.
missing-required-module.description: A package contract is missing a required module or public entry point. Explicit package contracts let contributors and agents follow the same structure. They apply only to matching packages and require no particular framework, feature layout or layer names. Excluded code does not fulfill a contract. This checks presence, not implementation quality. Repair: Implement the missing module in the matching package. If that package should follow a different structure, narrow or split the contract. Do not add empty implementation stubs solely to satisfy the check.
missing-required-module.markdownDescription:
**SMT307 — missing-required-module**

A package contract is missing a required module or public entry point.

Explicit package contracts let contributors and agents follow the same structure. They apply only to matching packages and require no particular framework, feature layout or layer names. Excluded code does not fulfill a contract. This checks presence, not implementation quality.

**Problem**
```yaml
structure:
  contracts:
    slices:
      match: app.slices.*
      required: [api]   # app.slices.orders.api is absent
```

**Preferred**
```yaml
structure:
  contracts:
    slices:
      match: app.slices.*
      required: [api]   # every matching package has an api module or package
```

Implement the missing module in the matching package. If that package should follow a different structure, narrow or split the contract. Do not add empty implementation stubs solely to satisfy the check.

Run `smelt explain missing-required-module` for details.

import-style.title: SMT308: An import does not follow the package's declared relative/absolute style.
import-style.description: An import does not follow the package's declared relative/absolute style. A predictable import style makes ownership easier to read. With relative style and max_relative_level: 1, local imports use one dot; parent and cross-root imports stay absolute. Deeper relative imports can be explicitly allowed. The closest package contract supplies the style. No style is enforced without an explicit contract, and this rule never changes bindings. Repair: Use a relative import within the configured dot limit, otherwise use an absolute import. Preserve aliases and update references if converting an import statement changes its binding. There is no automatic rewrite.
import-style.markdownDescription:
**SMT308 — import-style**

An import does not follow the package's declared relative/absolute style.

A predictable import style makes ownership easier to read. With relative style and max_relative_level: 1, local imports use one dot; parent and cross-root imports stay absolute. Deeper relative imports can be explicitly allowed. The closest package contract supplies the style. No style is enforced without an explicit contract, and this rule never changes bindings.

**Problem**
```python
# app/storage/service.py, relative style with maximum 1
from app.storage.models import Record
from ..domain import Entity
```

**Preferred**
```python
# app/storage/service.py
from .models import Record
from app.domain import Entity
```

Use a relative import within the configured dot limit, otherwise use an absolute import. Preserve aliases and update references if converting an import statement changes its binding. There is no automatic rewrite.

Run `smelt explain import-style` for details.

forbidden-module-docstring.title: SMT309: A module docstring is forbidden by the package's explicit convention.
forbidden-module-docstring.description: A module docstring is forbidden by the package's explicit convention. Some projects keep module descriptions in their architecture documentation. This opt-in convention checks the module's initial docstring, not function or class documentation or ordinary strings. Repair: Remove or move the module introduction according to the package's policy. No documentation is deleted automatically.
forbidden-module-docstring.markdownDescription:
**SMT309 — forbidden-module-docstring**

A module docstring is forbidden by the package's explicit convention.

Some projects keep module descriptions in their architecture documentation. This opt-in convention checks the module's initial docstring, not function or class documentation or ordinary strings.

**Problem**
```python
"""Redundant module introduction."""
VALUE = 1
```

**Preferred**
```python
VALUE = 1

def calculate():
    """Explain the calculation contract."""
```

Remove or move the module introduction according to the package's policy. No documentation is deleted automatically.

Run `smelt explain forbidden-module-docstring` for details.

forbidden-future-annotations.title: SMT310: The annotations future import violates a package or Python-version policy.
forbidden-future-annotations.description: The annotations future import violates a package or Python-version policy. An explicit source convention can forbid this import. In when-needed mode, a declared Python 3.14+ minimum also makes it a violation because annotations are already deferred by default. The future import still changes runtime representation, so removal requires checking annotation consumers and never happens automatically. Repair: Follow the declared convention while preserving forward references and runtime behavior. When-needed mode gives review hints on earlier or unknown targets and rejects the import on declared Python 3.14+ targets. An explicit allow exception can retain a runtime compatibility contract. No automatic rewrite is performed.
forbidden-future-annotations.markdownDescription:
**SMT310 — forbidden-future-annotations**

The annotations future import violates a package or Python-version policy.

An explicit source convention can forbid this import. In when-needed mode, a declared Python 3.14+ minimum also makes it a violation because annotations are already deferred by default. The future import still changes runtime representation, so removal requires checking annotation consumers and never happens automatically.

**Problem**
```python
from __future__ import annotations

VALUE = 1
```

**Preferred**
```python
VALUE = 1
```

Follow the declared convention while preserving forward references and runtime behavior. When-needed mode gives review hints on earlier or unknown targets and rejects the import on declared Python 3.14+ targets. An explicit allow exception can retain a runtime compatibility contract. No automatic rewrite is performed.

Run `smelt explain forbidden-future-annotations` for details.

unnecessary-future-annotations.title: SMT311: Review an annotations future import with no detected postponement need.
unnecessary-future-annotations.description: Review an annotations future import with no detected postponement need. third-party-denied.title: SMT103: A layer imports a third-party package its `third_party` policy does not allow.
third-party-denied.description: A layer imports a third-party package its `third_party` policy does not allow. Inner layers should not know about frameworks, drivers or SDKs. Keeping them out makes the core portable and cheap to test. With architecture.imports.transitive, the importing layer's policy also applies to packages reached through project modules, such as domain -> shared.utils -> sqlalchemy. A shortest chain includes each import's source line. External packages are leaves: their own source is not scanned. Standard-library imports remain allowed. Repair: Move the code that needs the package into a layer that allows it and expose it through a port, or extend the layer's `third_party` policy.

import-cycle.title: SMT104: Import cycles between features, between layers, or between sibling modules.
import-cycle.description: Import cycles between features, between layers, or between sibling modules. Cycles mean two parts can only be understood, tested and changed together. They also cause import-order bugs at runtime, unless one edge is imported only under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`; such cycles are marked `(type checking only)`. Imports that other rules already forbid (SMT101, SMT102, SMT106) and outbound imports from declared wiring are left out, so a cycle report means the cycle is built entirely from ordinary allowed dependencies. Repair: Break one edge of the cycle: extract the shared piece into a module both can import, invert one dependency behind an abstraction, or merge the parts.

**SMT104 — import-cycle**

Imports that other rules already forbid (SMT101, SMT102, SMT106) and outbound imports from declared wiring are left out, so a cycle report means the cycle is built entirely from ordinary allowed dependencies.

**Problem**
```python

# voice/application/calls.py

```

**Preferred**


package-import-fanout.title: SMT108: One caller imports many implementation modules of the same package.
package-import-fanout.description: One caller imports many implementation modules of the same package. Repeated imports of neighboring implementation modules can indicate a missing package API. This is an opt-in design hint, not proof of poor architecture. Count distinct target modules per source file and contracted package, not statements, symbols, or imports across the whole repository. Repair: Consider exporting the caller's supported API from the package facade. Check dependency direction and cycles before changing exports. If these independent dependencies are intentional, retain them or adjust the advisory threshold. Declare public: ['.'] to enforce facade-only imports.
package-import-fanout.markdownDescription:

**Problem**
```python

from app.users.application.update_user import UpdateUser
from app.users.application.delete_user import DeleteUser
```

**Preferred**

missing-required-module.title: SMT307: A package contract is missing a required module or public entry point.
missing-required-module.description: A package contract is missing a required module or public entry point. Explicit package contracts let contributors and agents follow the same structure. They apply only to matching packages and require no particular framework, feature layout or layer names. Excluded code does not fulfill a contract. This checks presence, not implementation quality. Repair: Implement the missing module in the matching package. If that package should follow a different structure, narrow or split the contract. Do not add empty implementation stubs solely to satisfy the check.
missing-required-module.markdownDescription:
**SMT307 — missing-required-module**

A package contract is missing a required module or public entry point.

Explicit package contracts let contributors and agents follow the same structure. They apply only to matching packages and require no particular framework, feature layout or layer names. Excluded code does not fulfill a contract. This checks presence, not implementation quality.

**Problem**
```yaml
structure:
  contracts:
    slices:
      match: app.slices.*
      required: [api]   # app.slices.orders.api is absent
```

**Preferred**
```yaml
structure:
  contracts:
    slices:
      match: app.slices.*
      required: [api]   # every matching package has an api module or package
```

import-style.title: SMT308: An import does not follow the package's declared relative/absolute style.
import-style.description: An import does not follow the package's declared relative/absolute style. A predictable import style makes ownership easier to read. With relative style and max_relative_level: 1, local imports use one dot; parent and cross-root imports stay absolute. Deeper relative imports can be explicitly allowed. The closest package contract supplies the style. No style is enforced without an explicit contract, and this rule never changes bindings. Repair: Use a relative import within the configured dot limit, otherwise use an absolute import. Preserve aliases and update references if converting an import statement changes its binding. There is no automatic rewrite.
import-style.markdownDescription:
**SMT308 — import-style**

A predictable import style makes ownership easier to read. With relative style and max_relative_level: 1, local imports use one dot; parent and cross-root imports stay absolute. Deeper relative imports can be explicitly allowed. The closest package contract supplies the style. No style is enforced without an explicit contract, and this rule never changes bindings.

**Problem**
```python

from ..domain import Entity
```

**Preferred**

forbidden-future-annotations.title: SMT310: The annotations future import violates a package or Python-version policy.
forbidden-future-annotations.description: The annotations future import violates a package or Python-version policy. An explicit source convention can forbid this import. In when-needed mode, a declared Python 3.14+ minimum also makes it a violation because annotations are already deferred by default. The future import still changes runtime representation, so removal requires checking annotation consumers and never happens automatically. Repair: Follow the declared convention while preserving forward references and runtime behavior. When-needed mode gives review hints on earlier or unknown targets and rejects the import on declared Python 3.14+ targets. An explicit allow exception can retain a runtime compatibility contract. No automatic rewrite is performed.

unnecessary-future-annotations.title: SMT311: Review an annotations future import with no detected postponement need.
unnecessary-future-annotations.description: Review an annotations future import with no detected postponement need. On targets before Python 3.14 or with an unknown minimum, when-needed mode retains imports for quoted and unresolved forward references, TYPE_CHECKING, runtime annotation inspection, decorated definitions and complex annotation expressions. Other cases get a conservative review hint, not proof of safe removal. Declared Python 3.14+ targets are handled by SMT310. Repair: Review whether postponement is part of the module's runtime contract, then remove unnecessary boilerplate and verify types and behavior. Keep the import if it serves a real purpose; annotate a justified exception if required.

no-private-modules.title: SMT312: A module or package has an underscore prefix forbidden by its naming policy.
no-private-modules.description: A module or package has an underscore prefix forbidden by its naming policy. Some projects use descriptive module names and keep private helpers inside them. This opt-in naming convention rejects _service.py and _internal/ even when they export public symbols. __init__.py and __main__.py retain their Python-defined roles. Function, method, class and attribute names are outside this rule. Architecture API contracts apply independently of the spelling of a module name. Repair: Choose a descriptive module or package name without a leading underscore, then update imports and deliberate facade exports. A more specific package can explicitly allow the convention. No files or symbols are renamed automatically.
no-private-modules.markdownDescription:
**SMT312 — no-private-modules**

A module or package has an underscore prefix forbidden by its naming policy.

Some projects use descriptive module names and keep private helpers inside them. This opt-in naming convention rejects _service.py and _internal/ even when they export public symbols. __init__.py and __main__.py retain their Python-defined roles. Function, method, class and attribute names are outside this rule. Architecture API contracts apply independently of the spelling of a module name.


public-definitions-first.title: SMT313: Definitions are out of public-first order within modeled execution boundaries.
public-definitions-first.description: Definitions are out of public-first order within modeled execution boundaries. Public interfaces should be easy to find. A stable topological order prioritizes configured categories while preserving category order, definition-time reads, rebinding and execution barriers. Function bodies are deferred; decorators, defaults, assignments and eager annotations are not. Future imports and declared Python 3.14+ targets defer annotations. Overload/property families remain atomic. Unknown execution is pinned. Repair: Review the expected order and execution barriers. Explicit check --fix can apply bounded moves where the package permits safe-only fixes. Imports, unknown execution and a misplaced main guard require manual review. Names and visibility are never rewritten by ordering. Refused sections identify the triggering expression and its source location in fix_blocker and fix_reason; the safety boundary stays in place.

bundled-instance-assignment.title: SMT314: An assignment writes multiple direct instance attributes under a separate-assignment convention.
bundled-instance-assignment.description: An assignment writes multiple direct instance attributes under a separate-assignment convention. Separate field assignments make object initialization easy to scan and extend. This opt-in package convention reports tuple/list unpacking and chained assignments that write multiple direct attributes of a method's first positional parameter, regardless of its name. It leaves local unpacking and single-field assignments alone. Recognized static/class methods and nested helper bodies are excluded; nested classes are inspected with their own receiver. This is a readability policy, not a logic error. Repair: Use one direct instance attribute write per statement. Preserve evaluation timing: unpack computed values into locals before assigning fields when appropriate. Parallel assignments, swaps, descriptors and unpacking failures can behave differently when split, so there is no automatic rewrite.
bundled-instance-assignment.markdownDescription:
**SMT314 — bundled-instance-assignment**

An assignment writes multiple direct instance attributes under a separate-assignment convention.

Separate field assignments make object initialization easy to scan and extend. This opt-in package convention reports tuple/list unpacking and chained assignments that write multiple direct attributes of a method's first positional parameter, regardless of its name. It leaves local unpacking and single-field assignments alone. Recognized static/class methods and nested helper bodies are excluded; nested classes are inspected with their own receiver. This is a readability policy, not a logic error.

**Problem**
```python
class Inbox:
    def __init__(self, log, control):
        self.log, self.control = log, control
```

**Preferred**
```python
class Inbox:
    def __init__(self, log, control):
        self.log = log
        self.control = control
```

Use one direct instance attribute write per statement. Preserve evaluation timing: unpack computed values into locals before assigning fields when appropriate. Parallel assignments, swaps, descriptors and unpacking failures can behave differently when split, so there is no automatic rewrite.

Run `smelt explain bundled-instance-assignment` for details.

prefer-match-type-dispatch.title: SMT315: Review a same-subject isinstance/elif chain for match/case under an explicit package policy.
prefer-match-type-dispatch.description: Review a same-subject isinstance/elif chain for match/case under an explicit package policy. Long type-dispatch chains can be clearer as class patterns and guards. This opt-in hint recognizes positive builtin isinstance tests over the same simple name, optionally followed by and guards. It preserves independent adjacent if statements and reports one candidate per whole supported chain. It is a readability suggestion, not proof of equivalent class-pattern behavior. Repair: Review class patterns, guards and subclass ordering. Preserve independent if statements, and keep nested body conditions inside their case: moving them into a case guard can introduce fallthrough. Match evaluates its subject once; custom instance checks, dynamic type expressions and side effects may differ. No automatic rewrite is performed. Declared Python minima before 3.10 are excluded; unknown minima require version review.
prefer-match-type-dispatch.markdownDescription:
**SMT315 — prefer-match-type-dispatch**

Review a same-subject isinstance/elif chain for match/case under an explicit package policy.

Long type-dispatch chains can be clearer as class patterns and guards. This opt-in hint recognizes positive builtin isinstance tests over the same simple name, optionally followed by and guards. It preserves independent adjacent if statements and reports one candidate per whole supported chain. It is a readability suggestion, not proof of equivalent class-pattern behavior.

**Problem**
```python
if isinstance(event, Started):
    start(event)
elif isinstance(event, Delta | Progress):
    update(event)
elif isinstance(event, Finished) and event.ok:
    finish(event)
```

**Preferred**
```python
match event:
    case Started():
        start(event)
    case Delta() | Progress():
        update(event)
    case Finished() if event.ok:
        finish(event)
```

Review class patterns, guards and subclass ordering. Preserve independent if statements, and keep nested body conditions inside their case: moving them into a case guard can introduce fallthrough. Match evaluates its subject once; custom instance checks, dynamic type expressions and side effects may differ. No automatic rewrite is performed. Declared Python minima before 3.10 are excluded; unknown minima require version review.

Run `smelt explain prefer-match-type-dispatch` for details.

internal-public-member.title: SMT316: A public module function or instance method has no observed use outside its module or class.
internal-public-member.description: A public module function or instance method has no observed use outside its module or class. An implementation helper should not advertise a public interface solely because it lacks a leading underscore. This opt-in package review includes unused definitions and internally used sync/async functions and ordinary instance methods. Imports and module escapes preserve module functions; known test accesses also count as external use, leaving test-only public functions to SMT429. Explicit module __all__ exports and decorated functions are preserved. Methods on decorated, inherited or subclassed classes, special/private methods, properties and class/static methods are excluded. For methods, even unresolved same-named attribute accesses outside the owning class conservatively preserve visibility. External libraries, frameworks, dynamic reflection and unscanned callers cannot be ruled out. This finding asks for review and does not prove a rename is safe. Excluded files, unselected packages and external consumers are unassessed; findings expose usage_scope so absence of observed callers is not mistaken for a whole-project proof. Repair: Review the supported interface and callers. For a genuine internal helper, add a leading underscore and update calls and callback references. Resolve existing private-name collisions before renaming. Preserve deliberate public APIs with __all__ for module functions or append `# smelt: ignore[SMT316] -- <specific API reason>` to the reported definition. Keep the concrete reason beside the code; Smelt cannot verify its truth. No automatic rename is performed.
internal-public-member.markdownDescription:
**SMT316 — internal-public-member**

A public module function or instance method has no observed use outside its module or class.

An implementation helper should not advertise a public interface solely because it lacks a leading underscore. This opt-in package review includes unused definitions and internally used sync/async functions and ordinary instance methods. Imports and module escapes preserve module functions; known test accesses also count as external use, leaving test-only public functions to SMT429. Explicit module __all__ exports and decorated functions are preserved. Methods on decorated, inherited or subclassed classes, special/private methods, properties and class/static methods are excluded. For methods, even unresolved same-named attribute accesses outside the owning class conservatively preserve visibility. External libraries, frameworks, dynamic reflection and unscanned callers cannot be ruled out. This finding asks for review and does not prove a rename is safe. Excluded files, unselected packages and external consumers are unassessed; findings expose usage_scope so absence of observed callers is not mistaken for a whole-project proof.

**Problem**
```python
class Browser:
    def emit(self, event): ...
    def run(self):
        self.emit('ready')
Browser().run()
```

**Preferred**
```python
class Browser:
    def _emit(self, event): ...
```
